header.running_head: The Piety and Scrupulousness of the Sahabah (RA)

blocks.text: Dujaanah, Qataadh, Salamah bin Akwa, Abu Hadrad, Khaalid bin Waleed, Baraa bin Maalik, Abu Mihjin, Ammaar bin Yaasir, Amr bin Ma'dikarib and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA).
The Piety and Scrupulousness of Our Guide Rasulullaah ﷺ

blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas (RA)
blocks.text: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas (RA) reports that one night Rasulullaah ﷺ found a date lying by his side and ate it. When he was unable to sleep that night, one of his wives asked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! You stayed awake all night?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "I ate a date that I found at my side and because we had the Sadaqah dates with us, I feared that this could be one of those."[^1]
The Piety and Scrupulousness of the Sahabah (RA)
The Piety and Scrupulousness of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA)

Hadhrat Muhammad bin Seereen says that besides Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA), he knows of no one who forcibly vomited out the food he had just eaten. Once after eating some food he had been served, someone informed him that the food had been provided by Hadhrat Ibn Nu'aymaan (RA). Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) exclaimed, "Were you feeding me the incantation fares of Ibn Nu'aymaan?!" He then forced himself to vomit.[^2]

blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla
blocks.text: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla reports that Hadhrat Ibn Nu'aymaan (RA) was an extremely handsome Sahabi. (During the Period of Ignorance) Some people once came to him asking if he knew anything that would help cure a woman who always miscarries. "Oh yes, I do," he replied. When they asked him what it was, he recited to them an incantation (which means):

"O disobedient womb!
Be still and stop spoiling blood
You are depriving her of bearing many children
If only these many children were in the disobedient womb
Because then she would bear them and recover"

In exchange for this, the people gave him a goat and some butter (after he had already become a Muslim). He then brought some of the meat to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA), who ate. However, (after being informed of the incident) Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) stood up and forced himself to vomit. He then reprimanded, "Why do you people bring me food without informing me where it has come from?!"[^3]
Ahmad, as quoted in Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.6 Pg.59).
Baghawi, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.360).
